sections.html:
Nebraska's Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act governs residential rentals. It begins at section 76-1401 of Chapter 76 and walks through the life of a tenancy: the rental agreement, deposits, repairs, entry, termination, and the lawsuit to get possession back.

If you own a rental and may sell, these sections matter most. Section 76-1416 covers security deposits and prepaid rent. Section 76-1417 requires disclosure of the manager and of the owner or owner's agent. Section 76-1419 makes the landlord keep the premises fit, and 76-1425 deals with landlord noncompliance. Section 76-1431 covers tenant noncompliance and failure to pay rent, 76-1434 bars landlord liens and distraint, and 76-1439 prohibits retaliation. Sections 76-1440 to 76-1447 run the action for possession from complaint to appeal.

Owners often ask whether listing a house ends a lease. These sections do not make a listing end a lease. Read the lease, and see an attorney before assuming a sale changes what a tenant is entitled to.

Section 76-1416(5) binds the person who holds the landlord's interest at the end of the tenancy to the deposit rules. So at closing, the seller and buyer should write down how the deposit passes over, and the buyer should know the exact amount.

The deposit rules are specific.

  • Prepaid rent and security go first to unpaid rent and to damage from the tenant's breach. Anything left goes back with a written itemization, and the deadline is fourteen days after the tenancy ends.
  • With no forwarding address, the landlord sends the balance and itemization by first-class mail to the last-known address.
  • Money that comes back undeliverable, or stays unclaimed for one year, is treated as abandoned property reported to the State Treasurer.
  • Missing that deadline can cost the landlord the deposit, court costs and reasonable attorney's fees. A willful failure not made in good faith adds liquidated damages: one month's rent or twice the deposit, whichever is less.

A cash buyer who inherits tenants will typically request the lease, the deposit figure and the payment ledger. Pulling them together early shortens the closing.

sections.h2: Telling the tenant who owns and manages the home
sections.html:
Under section 76-1417, the landlord or the person who signs for the landlord must hand the tenant two names and addresses in writing, no later than the start of the tenancy. The first is whoever is authorized to manage the premises. The second is an owner, or someone acting for the owner, who accepts service of process and gets notices and demands.

A change of owner can send rent and notices to the wrong place. The statute is written for the start of a tenancy and says nothing of handovers, yet seller and buyer should still put the new contact details in writing for the tenant, so rent and repair requests land where they should.

Section 76-1431 sets a short clock for unpaid rent and a longer one for other breaches. When rent is late, the landlord gives written notice of the nonpayment and of an intent to terminate. Seven calendar days without payment lets the landlord end the agreement.

A material breach, or one touching health and safety, calls for a written notice that names the acts or omissions. The agreement ends no sooner than thirty days after the tenant receives it, unless the tenant cures within fourteen days. Should substantially the same breach recur inside six months, fourteen days' written notice is enough to end it.

SituationWritten notice period
Rent unpaidSeven calendar days to pay
Material breach, first timeFourteen days to remedy; termination no sooner than thirty days after receipt
Same breach repeats within six monthsAt least fourteen days

Court comes after these notices. Section 25-21,221 also calls for notice to the adverse party three days before a forcible entry and detainer action starts. Tenants have remedies for unlawful ouster and exclusion under section 76-1430, which makes any shortcut around the courts a gamble.

sections.h2: When the landlord fails to keep the home livable
sections.html:
Tenants get a matching tool in section 76-1425. If the landlord materially fails the lease, or neglects the section 76-1419 repair duty in a way that hurts health and safety, the tenant can send a written list of the problems. Fourteen days without a fix ends the agreement on a date at least thirty days after the landlord gets the notice. A recurrence inside six months shortens that to at least fourteen days.

Put off repairs and you may face a tenant's claim just as a buyer's inspector arrives. Keep a written repair history, since it protects both sides. The act has separate sections on failure to supply heat, water and essential services (76-1427), fire or casualty damage (76-1429), and tenant remedies for unlawful ouster or diminished service (76-1430).

sections.h2: Retaliation and seizing a tenant's belongings
sections.html:
Neither is allowed, though limits apply. Section 76-1439 forbids a landlord from answering a code complaint, or tenants' union activity, with a rent hike, reduced services, or a possession suit or threat of one. The complaint must go to a government agency that enforces housing or building codes and concern a health or safety violation. The retaliated-against tenant gets section 76-1430 remedies and a defense to eviction. Reasonable rent increases and service changes are still permitted.

Section 76-1434 adds that a landlord's lien or security interest in a tenant's household goods cannot be enforced, and that distraint for rent is abolished. An owner preparing a rental for sale should never hold a tenant's property as leverage for unpaid rent.

The act also has special rules for tenants who are victims of domestic violence, including release from the rental agreement and lock changes (sections 76-1431.01 to 76-1431.04). Those rules stand apart from any sale.

The act sets its own court procedure for recovering possession. It runs from the action for possession in section 76-1440 through the complaint, summons, trial and writ of restitution, to appeal in section 76-1447. The Judicial Branch describes forcible entry and detainer as a proceeding to restore possession of land to a person who has been wrongfully deprived of it.

Owners who hold rentals through a company should note one rule. Outside Small Claims Court, a corporation or LLC landlord needs an attorney and cannot appear for itself.

With a case already open, speak to the attorney on it before signing a purchase agreement, and have the contract state whether the buyer takes the house occupied.

sections.h2: Preparing to sell with a tenant in place
sections.html:
A rental can sell with the tenant still inside, and paperwork in good order makes it easier. Try this list.

  • Pull the signed lease, any addenda, and the rent ledger.
  • Note the deposit, any pet deposit, and where the funds sit.
  • Make sure no notice of nonpayment or breach is half-finished, because the seven-day and thirty-day clocks run from written notice.
  • List open repair requests and complaints to a code office, since the retaliation rules apply.
  • At closing, hand the tenant written contact details for the new owner and manager.

A tenant behind on rent or a house needing work need not stop you, since an as-is buyer takes the property in its current condition. Cash Home Buyers makes cash offers on Nebraska houses like that. Nothing on this page is legal advice.

faqs.q: How much can a Nebraska landlord charge for a pet deposit?
faqs.a: A pet deposit may be up to one-fourth of one month's periodic rent (section 76-1416). That sits beside a security deposit capped at one month's rent. Housing agencies under the Nebraska Housing Agency Act are not subject to the cap.

faqs.q: How long does a landlord have to give notice for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Seven calendar days, counted from written notice of nonpayment and of the intent to terminate. Section 76-1431 then lets the landlord terminate if rent is still unpaid.

faqs.q: Who gets the deposit if the landlord sells?
faqs.a: Possibly the buyer. Deposit duties fall on whoever holds the landlord's interest at the end of the tenancy, so put the handling of the deposit in writing at closing.

faqs.q: Can a tenant be evicted for complaining to the city about conditions?
faqs.a: Not for that reason. Section 76-1439 bars retaliation, a possession suit or threat included, over a health or safety complaint to a code agency, although reasonable rent increases stay allowed.

faqs.q: Can an LLC landlord file an eviction case without a lawyer?
faqs.a: No. Except in Small Claims Court, a corporation or LLC landlord must be represented by an attorney.
